A weekend bread preorder form for Maya's regulars: they pick how many
sourdough, rye and cinnamon rolls they want, leave a name and phone number,
and press one button. Orders are saved instantly.

## What's on the page

- **The order form** — name, phone, and a number box for each of the three
  breads. Open Monday through Thursday night; from Friday it says orders
  are closed for the week (enforced on the server, in \`actor.ts\`).
- **"This week so far"** — what everyone can see: how many orders have come
  in and the running totals of each bread. No names, no phone numbers.
- **"For Maya — show my order list"** — a tucked-away box. Maya types her
  secret word and the full list appears: every order with name, phone and
  amounts, newest first, plus a **To bake** totals line and a
  **🖨️ Print orders** button (the printout shows only the orders: the date
  and "To bake" totals at the top, then one order per line).

Customer privacy is the point of the design: names and phone numbers never
leave the server without the secret word, which is checked in \`actor.ts\`
(\`BAKER_WORD\`) — never in the page. To change the word, change that one
line.

## How it's built

- \`index.html\` — the one page. \`main.ts\` runs it, \`styles.css\` styles it
  (including the print layout).
- \`actor.ts\` — the server half. Three actions: \`order\` (save an order),
  \`orders\` (public tally, no personal data) and \`bakerList\` (the full
  list, secret word required).
- \`sql/001_items.sql\`, \`sql/002_orders.sql\` — the tables (orders: name,
  phone, amounts, time). Migrations run once per instance; never edit one
  that has run, add a new file.
